http://www.euronews.com/2026/09/03/gener.text: A senior Russian air force commander was shot twice at close range in the Saratov region on Wednesday morning, in the latest of a series of attacks against Russian military officers on its territory.An unidentified gunman on a motorbike fired twice at the officer as he was leaving a shop in the village of Probuzhdeniye in Engels district and fled. One bullet struck him in the face, the other in the torso.He was taken to hospital in serious condition before being airlifted to Moscow for further treatment.Telegram military blogger channels identified the injured man as Major General Nikolai Varpakhovich, commander of the 22nd Heavy Bomber Aviation Division of Russia's long-range aviation branch. Russian authorities have not officially identified him.The ASTRA Telegram channel noted that Probuzhdeniye is listed as one of Varpakhovich's registered addresses.The city of Engels — some 850 kilometres from Moscow — hosts the Engels-2 airbase, one of Russia's most significant strategic aviation facilities.Bombing a hospitalVarpakhovich has been charged in absentia by Ukrainian authorities over the 8 July 2024 missile strike on the Okhmatdyt children's hospital in Kyiv.Ukrainian investigators said he ordered the attack, which resulted in a Kh-101 cruise missile striking the hospital.Two people were killed and more than 30 injured, including nine children. The building was partially destroyed.Ukraine's Health Ministry said 627 children were receiving treatment at the hospital at the time of the strike.Ukraine's Security Service published a statement on 31 August saying it had compiled evidence against two Russian military officials.The second is Colonel Aleksandr Lutovinov, commander of a missile brigade in the 49th Combined Arms Army, who investigators said organised the 24 August 2024 missile strike on the Sapphire hotel complex in Kramatorsk.A security adviser for Reuters news agency was killed in that attack, and five journalists were wounded.The shooting in Engels is part of a series of gun and bomb attacks involving Russian military figures that has grown in recent weeks.On 1 August, five people were killed and at least 19 wounded in an explosion at the Balzi Rossi restaurant in Moscow.The presumed target was Colonel General Aleksandr Chaiko, commander-in-chief of the Russian Aerospace Forces, whom Ukrainian authorities have accused of organising massacres in Bucha following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in early 2022.Chaiko was also the commanding officer of Russian forces participating in the Syrian war on the side of ousted dictator Bashar al-Assad.On 13 August, Russian Navy Captain First Rank Robert Shagiev was killed by an explosion in a street in Sevastopol. He was formerly the commander of Ukraine's submarine Zaporizhzhia. Shagiev was allegedly killed by a Russian national.Last week, Air Force Lieutenant Colonel Sergei Sechkov was killed and his wife was taken to intensive care when an improvised explosive device planted in his car detonated in St Petersburg.He was reportedly part of a Russian unit accused of attacks on civilians on the Slobozhanshchyna front in northeastern Ukraine.

Photograph: Nam Y Huh/AP US universities Sexual assault reported at frat house near University of Chicago Alleged assault follows report of gang-rape at frat house at Cornell, which ignited national uproar and criticism online Uwa Ede-Osifo Wed 14 Oct 2026 19.32 EDT Last modified on Wed 14 Oct 2026 19.49 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A 21-year-old woman reported being sexually assaulted last weekend at a fraternity house near the University of Chicago , as Greek life nationwide faces renewed scrutiny for recurrent misconduct. The incident allegedly took place on Sunday at about 1.50am at the off-campus Alpha Epsilon Pi residence, according to a university daily crime log. In a police report obtained by the Chicago Sun-Times, the woman said she was “not fully conscious” when she was found partially undressed inside a bathroom with a man, who was also semi-nude. Fraternities are the most likely place for unwanted sexual contact. Should they be shut down? Read more She told police, according to the report, that a group had blocked her friends, at first, from entering the bathroom. A person of interest has been identified, according to university officials. The individual is not a student and has been banned from campus, they announced on Wednesday. No one is in custody, Chicago police said on Wednesday afternoon, adding that an investigation remains ongoing. Jonathan Pierce, a spokesperson for the fraternity, said on Wednesday there was no evidence its members had participated in the assault or were aware of it. “When AEPi members (there were several “sober monitors” during the party, including the chapter’s safety officer) became aware of the victim’s report, they offered assistance by providing food and water and even loaned a shirt to the victim as she reported being cold while she waited outside for emergency response,” Pierce said. “We are pleased that the alleged assailant has been identified and hope that the victim can find some solace in knowing that justice is being done.” The alleged assault follows a harrowing report of a gang-rape at a Cornell University fraternity house in 2024. Recent news of the purported attack ignited national uproar and criticism of the Ivy League school’s perceived leniency toward the alleged offenders. New York state prosecutors have reopened an investigation into the report. Under mounting backlash, Cornell has also suspended all fraternity parties for the remainder of the academic year, as it assesses the safety of its Greek societies. Last week, the University of Arizona took a similar move, halting all fraternity activity in the wake of several hazing and physical assault allegations, including accusations of a Greek organization coercing recruits into binge drinking and swallowing live goldfish. https://www.dw.com/en/italy-cuts-air-tra.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OJvB Air traffic was reduced at hubs across Italy, including Milan Bergamo Airport [FILE: March 10, 2026] Image: Tiziano Manzoni/LaPresse/ZUMA/picture alliance Advertisement Air travelers across Italy faced delays and cancellations on Friday because of a problem with the country's air traffic control systems. The ENAV air traffic control authority ruled out foul play such as a cyberattack, and said it was forced to introduce temporary restrictions of the volume of flights after identifying a data transmission problem. Major airports in cities like Rome and Milan warned of likely disruptions and advised passengers to check with their airlines. What did authorities say about the problem? ENAV said it first identified the issue overnight. It was forced to restrict the volume of flights at around 6 a.m. (0400 GMT/UTC) as the number of scheduled services increased. "We would like to inform you that this morning we guaranteed the greatest possible number of departures, including intercontinental flights," ENAV said. Shorter-distance services were more likely to be interrupted. "Despite the anomalies encountered on the data transmission network, we are deploying all available resources to minimize disruption and restore full operations as soon as possible," ENAV said. "We confirm an operational capacity of 50% of total air traffic, ensuring maximum safety at all times, which remains the Company's top priority." ENAV said it had ruled out the possibility of the disturbance being caused by "malicious acts." Rome airports operator ADR warned passengers that "flight delays and cancellations may occur" and advised passengers to contact their airline if uncertain. Milan airports company SEA issued a similar notice.
